dct_description_sm:
Core descriptions were completed as part of facies characterization and regional mapping studies of the Lower Cretaceous Mannville Group oil sands strata in the Athabasca and Cold Lake Oil Sands areas. Cores were described along with the regional work over a time period exceeding 20 years, done by various Alberta Geological Survey staff and contractors. Most of the cores were logged from the top of the McMurray (or top of the Wabiskaw C) unit down to the base of core, or just below the sub-Cretaceous unconformity, if that was intersected by the cored interval.

Stratigraphic picks were made from geophysical logs and from the lithologic core descriptions. In some areas, facies definition was at a broad scale; in other areas, at a finer scale, depending upon the purpose of the core logging. The facies classification scheme evolved over the decades of work, and appropriate schemes are given with the legends for the different core descriptions. Cores were described using successive versions of the software AppleCORE©, on Apple Macintosh computers. Older AppleCORE files were updated to newer software versions when possible. Some of the oldest archival electronic files could not be updated to the 2009 version of AppleCORE, and in these cases, the paper copies were scanned.

All core descriptions (paper and updated electronic versions) were converted to PDFs, for use with PC-supported platforms. For a number of cores, there are multiple records. These include those cores for which multiple descriptions exist (either by different workers, or by the same worker but at different times); or, alternatively, those cores for which the cored section is very thick, and the described section was split into different intervals. Core descriptions are not harmonized; but rather taken as originally described by individual workers. Where appropriate, current stratigraphic terminology has been added to the core description.
